title: Production of Large Numbers of Size-controlled Tumor Spheroids Using Microwell Plates
protocol: Calculate the number of cells needed for each well based on the desired spheroid size and number of microwells per plate.
Prepare AggreWell plates according to specifications, including the use of surfactant solutions as necessary.
Load calculated number of cells into wells with appropriate volume of culture medium.
Remove microwell plates from packaging in a sterile environment such as a laminar-flow biosafety cabinet.
Add 0.5 ml of 70% ethanol to each unused well, adding liquid at one side to reduce air bubbles.
Replace lid and incubate for 5 min with the lid on at room temperature.
Centrifuge for 2 min at 2,000 x g if there are large numbers of air bubbles.
Using a low-magnification inverted microscope, verify that bubbles have been removed from the microwells.
Aspirate ethanol and wash plate with sterile water or PBS for immediate use.
Alternatively, air-dry plate for storage.
Prepare microwell surface using a surfactant initially to ensure cells do not interact with the surface.
Compare spheroids generated with and without surfactant-coated microwells.
Add 0.5 ml of Rinsing Solution to each well.
Centrifuge for 2 min at 2,000 x g to remove bubbles.
Verify that bubbles have been removed from the microwells using a low-magnification inverted microscope.
Incubate for at least thirty minutes with the lid on at room temperature or overnight at 4 °C.
Wash plate with sterile water or PBS immediately prior to use.
Aspirate growth medium from flask.
Add 3 ml of trypsin to the flask.
Incubate cells for 5 min at 37°C.
Stop trypsin digestion by adding 3 ml of growth medium.
Take an aliquot for cell counting.
Transfer the remainder into a 15 ml centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 200 x g.
Count cells while the centrifugation is in progress.
Aspirate trypsin/medium mixture and replace with fresh growth medium based on required cell density.
Pass the cell suspension through a strainer to remove clumps (optional).
Centrifuge for 2 min at 2,000 x g to remove bubbles.
Verify bubbles have been removed from the microwells using a low-magnification inverted microscope.
Mix 0.4 ml of cell suspension at the required density into the appropriate container or well.
Gently mix by pipetting up and down to ensure even distribution without introducing air bubbles.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 200 x g.
Verify that the plate is balanced internally and against another plate to prevent uneven cell distribution.
Check for convection currents post-centrifugation; if present, consult manufacturer for lubrication of pivot points as needed.
Inspect cells under an inverted microscope to confirm clustering within microwells and even distribution across wells.
Incubate overnight at 37 °C.
Using an inverted microscope, observe the process of spheroid formation.
Recover spheroids from microwells by gently jetting them out with a pipette.
Alternatively, maintain spheroids in situ with medium replacement.
Aspirate medium at the edge of the well using a Pasteur pipette.
Slowly bring the tip down until it begins to draw liquid from the meniscus.
Follow the meniscus down as it drops.
Add fresh medium against the well wall in the same place.
